title: Jai's five boxing foundations
scope: A deeper lesson scaffold behind the 40-second mirror; not a completed boxing course.

methodology.design: CDF / Gagné-informed objectives, one-cue practice, evidence, reflection and transfer
methodology.teacherAuthority: Jai owns the mental model and lesson intent; reviewed video provides the technical cue.
methodology.validation: Structure and source linkage can be checked here. Physical technique and transfer need trainer/learner evidence.

metaphors.claim: A way to remember the hands as tools for action; not a literal weapon instruction.
A memory aid for guard awareness; not proof of protection or a validated catch technique.
A memory aid for movement; not a claim that feet should roll or slide in a particular way.
A memory aid for attention to head position. The head is not protective equipment; this metaphor claims no protection.

foundations.title: Calm attention and the body map

objectives.label: LEARNING_OBJECTIVE
objectives.observableBehavior: Given Jai’s body-map metaphor, describe one body part you chose to attend to and distinguish what you saw from what you felt.

concepts.label: CONCEPT
concepts.definition: A shared metaphor directs attention; your felt state belongs to your report.

practice.label: SKILL
practice.cue: Choose one part of your body to notice.
practice.instructions: Name one part of the body map. Before and after a brief observation, describe how settled or distracted you felt, in your own words.

assessments.label: ASSESSMENT_ITEM
assessments.prompt: What did you see, and what did you feel? Keep those as separate observations.

transfer.label: TRANSFER_CONTEXT
transfer.prompt: Take one observation to your coach and ask what to attend to in the next practice.

learningCircle.care: Choose what you want to notice.
learningCircle.try: Name one part of the body map. Before and after a brief observation, describe how settled or distracted you felt, in your own words.
learningCircle.neededConcept: A shared metaphor directs attention; your felt state belongs to your report.
learningCircle.artifact: Keep your observation and its source or video timestamp.
learningCircle.share: Choose whether to show a coach or peer; keep their response separate.
learningCircle.newQuestion: What would you like to notice next time?

visible2D: visible body-part position in a selected frame
evidencePolicy.feedback: Describe only the recorded evidence. Ask about felt experience; never infer it from pose.

gaps.detail: No reviewed breathing protocol or camera-based breath/calm assessment is established.

objectives.label: LEARNING_OBJECTIVE

concepts.label: CONCEPT
concepts.definition: The attempt includes the approach and exit, not only the punch.

sources.cue: Move before the punch. Move again after it.
sources.evidenceType: actual source video and burned-in instructions inspected

sources.cue: Pay more attention to your approach and exit than your punches.

practice.label: SKILL
practice.cue: Move before the punch. Move again after it.
practice.instructions: Watch the source approach and exit. In a no-contact shadowboxing adaptation, attend to your movement before and after one imagined touch; then review your own attempt.

assessments.label: ASSESSMENT_ITEM
assessments.prompt: Where in your attempt did you move before or after the touch? What would you try differently?

transfer.label: TRANSFER_CONTEXT

objectives.label: LEARNING_OBJECTIVE
objectives.observableBehavior: Given the reviewed forward-looking cue, distinguish your reported gaze from a visible head position and identify A/B as undefined until Jai supplies the distinction.

concepts.label: CONCEPT
concepts.definition: A visible head position, gaze direction and the learner’s attention are different kinds of evidence.

sources.cue: Start with rolls in one spot.
sources.evidenceType: visually inspected burned-in instruction and demonstration

sources.cue: Look forward rather than down or aside.
sources.evidenceType: reviewed video-section frames and automatic captions; audio not independently listened

practice.label: SKILL
practice.cue: Look forward rather than down or aside.
practice.instructions: Review the source’s forward-looking cue during defensive movement. Report where you were looking; do not infer gaze from pose. Ask Jai to define and demonstrate A and B before using those as movement commands.

assessments.label: ASSESSMENT_ITEM
assessments.prompt: Which head-position change can you actually see? What would you need Jai to show to distinguish A from B?

transfer.label: TRANSFER_CONTEXT
transfer.prompt: Bring the question and source timestamp to Jai or your coach; record their A/B definition before extending practice.
